Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Ley 19/2018, de 5 de diciembre, de transposición de las Directivas (UE) 2015/849 y 2016/2258; Real Decreto 609/2023, de 11 de julio, por el que se crea el Registro Central de Titularidades Reales (RCTR); Ley Orgánica 3/2018, de 5 de diciembre, de Protección de Datos Personales.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

Permissible only as a transitional substance arrangement provided the serviced or virtual office is a physically located Spanish address managed under an executed lease or service agreement, and the company's books, records, and management facilities can be produced at that address. A pure postal box or accommodation address does not satisfy the real-seat doctrine of Article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010) and will be treated by the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and SEPBLAC as a sham-seat indicator. For the licensed-free used-machinery wholesale activity, a serviced business-hub office (Madrid, Barcelona, or Valencia) is market-acceptable at inception, but the company should migrate to a leased warehouse or commercial office within the first operating year; corporate banks applying enhanced due diligence for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier normally require proof of a full lease or executive serviced-office agreement before onboarding.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

The competent authority is the Registro Mercantil of the province where the registered office is located. Name availability is obtained from the Registro Mercantil Central.

Governing statute

Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), approved by Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, particularly Articles 19-23, 28-30, 32-35, 58-63, 210-242, and 285-290. The Electronic and Digital Corporate Law reforms, including Law 18/2022, also apply to simplified and electronic formation procedures.

Formation / constitutional filings

Notarised public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), followed by an application for registration with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial).

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 48 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

A Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may be incorporated with minimum share capital of EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation; no statutory escrow account is required. Until the company reaches EUR 3,000 of capital plus legal reserves, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to the legal reserve until the combined amount reaches EUR 3,000. In liquidation, shareholders may be jointly liable for the difference between EUR 3,000 and the company's subscribed capital if the company cannot satisfy its liabilities. Notary and Mercantile Registry charges are separate regulated professional fees and are not included in the stated state filing fee.

Funding & unlock path: Before opening, obtain or file the municipal activity, opening, or responsible declaration required for the premises and demonstrate compliance with the Spanish Building Code, fire-safety rules under Royal Decree 513/2017, and applicable municipal fire requirements. Maintain emergency routes, extinguishers, fire detection and compartmentation where required, and obtain technical certificates or inspections for structural load and machinery areas. Comply with occupational risk-prevention duties under Law 31/1995, including risk assessment, worker training, personal protective equipment, lifting and traffic controls, and coordination with contractors. A separate industrial safety registration may apply if regulated installations, pressure equipment, fuel storage, or electrical installations are installed.

Paid-in capital rule: A Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may be incorporated with minimum share capital of EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation; no statutory escrow account is required. Until the company reaches EUR 3,000 of capital plus legal reserves, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to the legal reserve until the combined amount reaches EUR 3,000. In liquidation, shareholders may be jointly liable for the difference between EUR 3,000 and the company's subscribed capital if the company cannot satisfy its liabilities. Notary and Mercantile Registry charges are separate regulated professional fees and are not included in the stated state filing fee.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts and records the subscription and full payment of its issued share capital by the founding shareholder in accordance with the deed of incorporation; (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted and entered in the Company's records; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or, where applicable, the directors named in the deed are confirmed, each with the powers stated in the articles and applicable law; (4) the officers are authorised to obtain tax, municipal, banking, customs, and operational registrations and to execute all filings required to commence the Company's wholesale machinery activities.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Exempted / Not Required

The competent authority is generally the industry department of the autonomous community where the premises are located, together with the relevant municipal authority. The Ministry of Industry and Tourism is the national coordinating authority but normally does not issue a general wholesale machinery trading licence.

Category: No general national manufacturing or industrial operating licence is normally required for wholesale remarketing of used hydraulic excavators and rollers. A municipal activity licence, prior communication, or responsible declaration for the warehouse or commercial premises may be required under the applicable autonomous-community and municipal rules.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — official portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) first obtains a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) upon execution of the public incorporation deed before a notary; the definitive corporate NIF is then issued via Form 036/037 filed with the AEAT before commencement of activity. The SL, as a tax-resident company, is registered in the Censo de Obligados Tributarios under its corporate NIF. Non-resident foreign shareholders do not require a separate Spanish tax ID for the SL's incorporation; however, any foreign parent or related entity engaging in Spanish taxable transactions must obtain a NIF (letter 'N' regime) through Form 036 and, where required, appoint a tax representative resident in Spain. The SL's definitive NIF is thereafter used for all VAT, Corporate Income Tax, customs, and statistical reporting obligations.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation - Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades at the standard 25% rate on worldwide income as a tax resident; non-resident shareholders are taxed separately under the Non-Resident Income Tax regime, while the entity itself is not eligible for pass-through treatment under Spanish law. — A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) first obtains a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) upon execution of the public incorporation deed before a notary; the definitive corporate NIF is then issued via Form 036/037 filed with the AEAT before commencement of activity. The SL, as a tax-resident company, is registered in the Censo de Obligados Tributarios under its corporate NIF. Non-resident foreign shareholders do not require a separate Spanish tax ID for the SL's incorporation; however, any foreign parent or related entity engaging in Spanish taxable transactions must obtain a NIF (letter 'N' regime) through Form 036 and, where required, appoint a tax representative resident in Spain. The SL's definitive NIF is thereafter used for all VAT, Corporate Income Tax, customs, and statistical reporting obligations.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation - Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades at the standard 25% rate on worldwide income as a tax resident; non-resident shareholders are taxed separately under the Non-Resident Income Tax regime, while the entity itself is not eligible for pass-through treatment under Spanish law.

Available election forms

Spain does not operate a check-the-box or equivalent elective classification regime. Statutory elections available include the tax consolidation regime (grupo de consolidación fiscal) under Articles 61-80 of Ley 27/2014 (LIS), requiring 75% direct or indirect ownership and minimum 6-month shareholding; optional free-depreciation and accelerated-depreciation rules; R&D and technological innovation tax-credit elections; the participation-exemption election for qualifying foreign dividends and capital gains; and the tonnage-tax regime for qualifying shipping groups. Hybrid-mismatch corrective rules under ATAD/DAC are mandatorily applied via LIS Articles 15 bis and 18 bis, with no elective opt-out.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general economic-turnover threshold for VAT registration: registration is mandatory before the first taxable supply under Ley 37/1992 (LIVA). The simplified-regime (régimen simplificado) is available only for qualifying small businesses with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 250,000; retailers may use the equivalence-surcharge regime (recargo de equivalencia) up to EUR 150,000 annual turnover. For the wholesale remarketing of used construction excavators, the principal registration obligation is the ordinary censal declaration via Form 036 prior to any transaction.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of used hydraulic earthmovers and rollers to non-EU destinations qualify for 0% VAT with full deduction of input VAT under LIVA Article 21, provided the goods physically leave EU territory within 3 months of dispatch and the exporter retains adequate proof of export. Intra-Community supplies to a VAT-registered customer in another Member State are exempt under LIVA Article 25 if the customer's valid VIES identification number is obtained and the goods are transported out of Spain to another Member State. Export transactions are zero-rated irrespective of the used-goods margin scheme under Article 128 LIVA; however, the exporter must obtain the export evidence within the applicable legal deadline and include the supplies in the periodic VAT return and recapitulative statement (Form 349) where applicable.

  • Customs Export Declaration (Documento Único Administrativo / DUA) with MRN number
  • Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR international consignment note evidencing physical departure from Spain/EU territory
  • Commercial invoice, pro-forma invoice, and, if used, sales contract or purchase order for the used machinery
  • Packing list with machine identification and serial numbers matching the DUA
  • Proof of delivery at destination signed by the non-EU customer or carrier
  • Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103 credit advice, or bank statement evidencing receipt of export payment
  • Intrastat dispatch declaration if goods move to another EU Member State
  • Documentation of the supplier's VAT registration and VIES validation where an intra-Community supply exemption is claimed

Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing is introduced by Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), phased in from 2024-2025, requiring interoperable e-invoice formats. Large taxpayers with turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000 and VAT groups must submit all invoice records to AEAT in near real time under the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) system within 4 calendar days of issuance; the Verifactu Regulation (Real Decreto 1007/2023) requires the use of AEAT-compliant billing software with QR-code and hash-chain features by all applicable taxpayers from 2025. Customs export declarations are filed electronically via the DUES (Declaración Única Administrativa) / Sumisi贸n EDI system operated by the Agencia Tributaria's Customs Department.

AEAT may retrospectively claw back all input VAT deducted on zero-rated exports if the export is not fully documented within the statutory records, adding late-payment interest under Article 191 LGT. Infringements under LIVA Article 170 attract fixed penalties of EUR 300 to EUR 6,000 per invoice per unit, or proportional penalties of 50%-150% of the undeclared tax; knowingly fraudulent export zero-rating or false export documentation constitutes criminal tax fraud under Article 305 and 305 bis of the Spanish Criminal Code where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, punishable by imprisonment of 1 to 6 years, fines of up to six times the defrauded amount, and loss of tax benefits or public subsidies. Customs declaration errors additionally trigger sanctions under Real Decreto 328/2018 (Reglamento General de Actuaciones y Procedimientos de Gestión e Inspección Tributaria), and refund claims may be refused or suspended where the exporter fails to provide coherent and verifiable export evidence.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain uses the euro and has a fully liberalized current-account and capital-account regime subject to EU and Spanish anti-money-laundering, sanctions, tax, prudential, and statistical-reporting rules. A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may generally receive foreign capital, convert funds, pay suppliers, distribute dividends, repay qualifying shareholder loans, and remit profits without prior foreign-exchange approval. Banks may require evidence of the commercial purpose, beneficial ownership, source of funds, underlying contracts, tax compliance, and sanctions screening. Dividend distributions require distributable profits, approval under Spanish corporate law, maintenance of legally required reserves, and documentation of applicable Spanish withholding tax or treaty relief. Interest, royalties, management fees, and related-party payments require arm's-length support, transfer-pricing documentation, withholding-tax analysis, and beneficial-owner evidence. Non-resident foreign investments, acquisitions, disposals, and certain changes in ownership may trigger declarations to the Ministry of Economy, including filings under Royal Decree 571/2023 and its implementing rules. Certain foreign investments in strategic sectors, or investments involving regulated or security-sensitive activities, may require prior authorization; ordinary wholesale trading of used excavators and rollers is not ordinarily a strategic-sector activity, but the facts should be screened before closing.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a Spanish bank, convert a mandatory percentage of export receipts into euros, or complete conversion within a prescribed export-receipt deadline. Export proceeds may generally be retained in foreign currency or received into an eligible euro or foreign-currency account, subject to banking, tax, customs, sanctions, and accounting controls. The company must retain commercial invoices, customs or transport evidence where applicable, purchase orders, bills of lading, delivery evidence, and payment records. Cross-border payment and external-position information may be reportable through Banco de España statistical reporting systems, particularly for entities meeting applicable reporting thresholds or receiving specific reporting requests. Export VAT treatment, customs declarations, Intrastat obligations where applicable, and tax records remain separate from foreign-exchange rules. Cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more when entering or leaving the EU, and certain domestic cash movements of EUR 100,000 or more, are subject to Spanish declaration requirements; banks may also impose transaction-level monitoring and documentary requirements.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España, acting within the Eurosystem under the authority of the European Central Bank. Foreign-investment reporting is principally administered by the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise under Spain's foreign-investment regulations. Spain applies the EU framework for payment services, capital movements, sanctions, anti-money laundering, and financial-market conduct.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium. An EU-authorized electronic money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, SEPA transfers, foreign-exchange services, and international payment execution through passporting or an authorized Spanish branch or agent, subject to its license perimeter and local registration status. An electronic money account is not a bank deposit and does not provide the same deposit-guarantee protection as a credit institution; customer funds must be safeguarded under the applicable payment-services rules. An offshore non-EU EMI generally cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to Spanish customers solely through an offshore website without an appropriate EU authorization, passport, branch, agent, or other legally valid access route. Fintechs may reject used-heavy-machinery trading because of sanctions exposure, high-value goods, complex logistics, third-country counterparties, unusual payment corridors, cash intensity, or insufficient transaction history. The Spanish SL should retain at least one fully regulated Spanish or EEA credit-institution relationship for payroll, taxes, customs, trade finance, and contingency liquidity.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner with an opaque ownership chain, nominee arrangement, trust, bearer-share history, or inconsistent ownership information

Root cause: Non-resident shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner with an opaque ownership chain, nominee arrangement, trust, bearer-share history, or inconsistent ownership information

Defense evidence: Current commercial-register extracts for every intermediate entity; certified constitutional documents; complete ownership chart to each natural-person beneficial owner; passports and proof of address; beneficial-owner declaration; board and shareholder resolutions; notarized or apostilled powers of attorney; explanation of control rights; and a written confirmation that no nominee, bearer-share, or undisclosed controlling arrangement exists.
Foreign capital injection with unexplained source of funds, round-sum transfers, third-party remitters, or payment from an account not held by the shareholder

Root cause: Foreign capital injection with unexplained source of funds, round-sum transfers, third-party remitters, or payment from an account not held by the shareholder

Defense evidence: Share subscription or capital-increase resolution; bank transfer confirmation from the shareholder's account; shareholder bank statements; audited financial statements; tax returns or sale agreements supporting wealth origin; loan agreement where funding is debt; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth memorandum; beneficial-owner evidence; and reconciliation between the incoming amount, accounting entry, and corporate-register filing.
Used construction machinery activity involving high-value assets, cash purchases, unusual price discounts, rapid resale, multiple intermediaries, or counterparties in higher-risk jurisdictions

Root cause: Used construction machinery activity involving high-value assets, cash purchases, unusual price discounts, rapid resale, multiple intermediaries, or counterparties in higher-risk jurisdictions

Defense evidence: Detailed business plan; inventory and asset-identification procedure; serial-number and ownership checks; invoices; purchase and resale contracts; valuation methodology; transport and delivery records; customs documents; sanctions and restricted-party screening policy; anti-bribery policy; payment policy prohibiting unexplained third-party payments and excessive cash; customer and supplier due-diligence files; and sample transaction-flow map.
Payment corridors involving sanctioned countries, sanctioned persons, embargo-sensitive goods, military end users, or potentially dual-use machinery

Root cause: Payment corridors involving sanctioned countries, sanctioned persons, embargo-sensitive goods, military end users, or potentially dual-use machinery

Defense evidence: Counterparty KYC; end-user and end-use certificates; export-control classification; EU and UN sanctions screening records; transport-route analysis; customs classification; licensing or non-licensing determination; contractual sanctions clauses; independent compliance review; and documented escalation and rejection procedures. No transaction should proceed where applicable sanctions or export-control authorization is absent.
Mismatch between declared business activity, expected turnover, account geography, payment currencies, and actual transaction behavior

Root cause: Mismatch between declared business activity, expected turnover, account geography, payment currencies, and actual transaction behavior

Defense evidence: Board-approved treasury policy; twelve-month cash-flow forecast; country and currency matrix; expected monthly transaction volumes; supplier and customer list; representative contracts and invoices; warehouse or logistics agreements; VAT and tax-registration evidence; payroll and operating-cost budget; and quarterly account-monitoring review signed by management.
Reliance on offshore digital EMIs, virtual IBANs, payment intermediaries, or nested accounts for core operating activity

Root cause: Reliance on offshore digital EMIs, virtual IBANs, payment intermediaries, or nested accounts for core operating activity

Defense evidence: Provider authorization and passporting evidence; account-holder and safeguarding disclosures; contractual terms; explanation of each payment intermediary; transaction-flow chart; reconciliation controls; proof that the account is in the company's legal name; contingency banking plan; and confirmation that regulated banking, tax, customs, payroll, and trade-finance obligations will not be bypassed.
Beneficial owner, director, authorized signatory, or major counterparty identified as a politically exposed person or associated person

Root cause: Beneficial owner, director, authorized signatory, or major counterparty identified as a politically exposed person or associated person

Defense evidence: PEP disclosure; role and appointment history; enhanced source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; independent adverse-media search; government salary, asset, tax, or business-interest evidence where appropriate; risk-based approval by senior management; enhanced transaction monitoring; and documented absence of bribery, corruption, or public-procurement conflicts.
Incomplete Spanish corporate records, missing tax identification number, inconsistent registered address, or inability to verify operating substance

Root cause: Incomplete Spanish corporate records, missing tax identification number, inconsistent registered address, or inability to verify operating substance

Defense evidence: Notarial deed of incorporation; current Registro Mercantil extract; Spanish tax identification certificate; registered office evidence; lease, warehouse, or logistics agreement; director and signatory appointments; shareholder register or ownership statement; municipal or sector registration where relevant; invoices and contracts; and evidence of actual management and operational decision-making.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Route equity through a regulated Spanish or EEA credit institution into the SL's corporate account, with the remitter named exactly as the subscribing shareholder or documented lender. Use a clear transfer narrative such as 'capital contribution', 'share subscription', 'capital increase', or 'shareholder loan', supported by the relevant shareholder and board resolutions. For SWIFT payments, provide accurate ordering-customer, beneficiary, ultimate-beneficiary, and purpose information; do not use personal accounts, undisclosed third parties, cash, or payment agents. For an incorporation or capital increase, obtain the bank's capital-deposit certificate where required by the notary and corporate-registration process, then transfer funds to the operational account after registration. Reconcile the bank credit to the accounting ledger and corporate filing. Review foreign-investment declaration requirements under Royal Decree 571/2023 and applicable Ministry of Economy forms, including any threshold, sector, ownership-change, or periodic reporting obligation. Retain bank advices, resolutions, subscription documents, loan agreements, source-of-funds evidence, tax records, and foreign-exchange reporting evidence. SEPA transfers are appropriate for euro-denominated EEA payments; SWIFT is appropriate for non-SEPA or multi-currency payments. Banks may request a payment purpose, supporting documents, and beneficial-owner verification even though Spain has no general capital-control approval process.Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area, subject to bank limits and fraud controls. Use SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly evidenced by an MT103 or its ISO 20022 successor message, for non-SEPA or foreign-currency supplier payments; include complete originator, beneficiary, bank, invoice, goods description, and purpose information. For substantial machinery imports, use an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit, preferably subject to UCP 600, with presentation conditions covering commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, insurance where required, inspection certificate, serial numbers, origin evidence, and sanctions or end-user representations. Consider documentary collection under URC 522 for lower-risk counterparties, and open-account terms only after credit and sanctions due diligence. Match each payment to a purchase order, invoice, contract, customs or transport record, and goods-receipt evidence. Verify beneficiary bank-account changes through an independent channel. Avoid third-party payments unless approved, documented, and accepted by the bank. Apply VAT, customs, withholding-tax, transfer-pricing, and import-control analysis separately from the payment-clearing decision. Maintain segregation of duties for payment initiation, approval, sanctions screening, and bank reconciliation.Deliverable forward exchange contracts with an authorized bank or investment firm to hedge documented forecast or committed EUR, USD, GBP, or other foreign-currency machinery purchases and sales. The notional, tenor, currency, and maturity should be proportionate to identifiable commercial exposure.Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity and currency-management purposes, subject to counterparty credit limits, documented commercial exposure, collateral terms, and treasury approval.Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency is non-convertible or market convention requires cash settlement. NDFs do not create a route around Spanish, EU, sanctions, tax, or capital-movement rules and should be entered only with an appropriately authorized counterparty.Currency options and collars may be used for documented trade exposures where the company understands premium, settlement, break-cost, and potential-obligation risks. The company should avoid speculative or leveraged structures unrelated to its operating exposure.Cross-currency swaps may be appropriate for material, longer-term shareholder or bank financing, subject to counterparty documentation, valuation, collateral, accounting, and interest-rate risk controls.Hedging documentation should specify the exposure, hedge ratio, authorized counterparties, ISDA or equivalent master documentation, confirmations, collateral and margin obligations, valuation controls, accounting treatment under applicable Spanish GAAP or IFRS, EMIR-related reporting and risk-mitigation requirements where applicable, and periodic effectiveness review. Derivatives involving an EU investment firm or bank remain subject to MiFID II, EMIR, market-conduct, suitability or appropriateness, reporting, and prudential requirements as applicable.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium. An EU-authorized electronic money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, SEPA transfers, foreign-exchange services, and international payment execution through passporting or an authorized Spanish branch or agent, subject to its license perimeter and local registration status. An electronic money account is not a bank deposit and does not provide the same deposit-guarantee protection as a credit institution; customer funds must be safeguarded under the applicable payment-services rules. An offshore non-EU EMI generally cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to Spanish customers solely through an offshore website without an appropriate EU authorization, passport, branch, agent, or other legally valid access route. Fintechs may reject used-heavy-machinery trading because of sanctions exposure, high-value goods, complex logistics, third-country counterparties, unusual payment corridors, cash intensity, or insufficient transaction history. The Spanish SL should retain at least one fully regulated Spanish or EEA credit-institution relationship for payroll, taxes, customs, trade finance, and contingency liquidity.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general Spanish Corporate Income Tax rate. Newly incorporated entities generally apply a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and eligibility conditions.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish resident company to a non-resident recipient, subject to exemptions, treaty relief, beneficial-ownership requirements, anti-abuse rules, and domestic exemptions.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Modelo 200: within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year company closing on 31 December, the normal filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year, subject to electronic-filing and banking-calendar rules. Modelo 202: generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December; the final day is normally extended where the payment is made by direct debit under AEAT rules.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally 1 to 20 April, 1 to 20 October, and 1 to 20 December. Large companies and companies using the current-period method may be subject to additional calculation requirements and mandatory electronic payment procedures.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: No single universal Spanish threshold triggers all transfer-pricing documentation. A Spanish Local File is generally required for material related-party transactions, subject to statutory exemptions and simplified documentation. The commonly relevant exemption is that documentation is not required for transactions with the same related person or entity of the same type and under the same valuation method where the aggregate market value does not exceed EUR 250,000 in the relevant tax period, subject to exclusions for specific transactions. A Master File is generally required for Spanish entities belonging to a group with consolidated turnover of at least EUR 45 million, subject to statutory exceptions. Country-by-Country reporting generally applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a separate standalone regime titled Economic Substance Regulations comparable to certain offshore jurisdictions. Economic substance is nevertheless relevant through the general anti-abuse rule, the conflict-in-application doctrine, the principal-purpose rule in treaties, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, transfer-pricing requirements, interest limitation, anti-hybrid rules, and EU anti-tax-avoidance legislation. The SL should maintain genuine Spanish management, decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or logistics capability proportionate to its used-heavy-machinery wholesale activity, commercial risk control, inventory and customs records, and banking and accounting substance. A conduit company receiving dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees without commercial functions is exposed to denial of treaty or domestic relief and reassessment.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Corporate Income Tax evasion and false tax reporting

Statutory sanction: Administrative tax penalties commonly range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, with interest and collection measures. Tax fraud may become a criminal offence where the evaded tax exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period. Basic tax fraud may carry imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of 1 to 6 times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or organized or particularly sophisticated conduct, may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of 2 to 6 times the amount defrauded.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto managers may incur civil and tax liability where they deliberately participate, negligently fail to prevent the breach, or cause the company to become non-compliant. Criminal conviction can lead to imprisonment, fines, disqualification from public office or management, asset seizure, and restitution. Travel restrictions may be imposed by a court in criminal or enforcement proceedings; they are not an automatic consequence of an ordinary tax adjustment.
Value Added Tax and customs fraud

Statutory sanction: VAT and customs assessments may include unpaid tax, late-payment interest, confiscation or seizure of goods, and administrative penalties commonly calculated by reference to the unpaid or improperly claimed amount. Serious or organized VAT fraud may also satisfy the criminal tax-fraud threshold.

Director personal liability: Directors may face joint or subsidiary liability, criminal prosecution for intentional fraud, asset seizure, and disqualification where they direct or knowingly facilitate the conduct.
Transfer-pricing manipulation

Statutory sanction: AEAT may make a primary adjustment, impose compensating adjustments where legally available, deny deductions, recharacterize distributions, and impose transfer-pricing documentation penalties. Documentation breaches may attract fixed penalties per omitted or incorrect data point, while underpaid tax may attract percentage-based penalties and interest.

Director personal liability: Directors may face tax liability and civil claims for deliberate or grossly negligent conduct, especially where the arrangement lacks commercial purpose or causes insolvency. Criminal exposure generally requires intentional conduct meeting the statutory tax-fraud threshold.
Shell company, treaty abuse, and beneficial-ownership failure

Statutory sanction: Treaty or domestic withholding relief may be denied, with recovery of withholding tax, interest, surcharges, and penalties. The arrangement may be challenged under Spanish anti-abuse provisions, the principal-purpose rule, beneficial-ownership standards, or the general anti-avoidance doctrine.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur civil and tax liability and, where fraud is intentional and material, criminal liability. Courts may order asset freezing, confiscation, management disqualification, and restitution. A travel ban requires judicial grounds and is not automatic.
Anti-money laundering and sanctions compliance

Statutory sanction: Spanish AML breaches may result in warnings, public reprimands, license or activity restrictions where applicable, and administrative fines that can reach the statutory maximums applicable to the breach, including material percentage-based or fixed penalties. Money laundering may constitute a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment, fines, and confiscation.

Director personal liability: Directors and compliance officers may be personally liable for intentional participation or serious organizational failures. Criminal money-laundering liability can include imprisonment, fines, disqualification, asset confiscation, and judicial restrictions on movement.
Accounting, corporate records, and insolvency misconduct

Statutory sanction: Consequences may include rejection of accounts, tax reassessment, civil damages, restoration of assets, insolvency clawback, director disqualification, and criminal liability for falsification, creditor frustration, or aggravated insolvency misconduct.

Director personal liability: Directors may be ordered to cover all or part of the insolvency deficit, return improperly distributed funds, compensate creditors, and bear civil or criminal sanctions. The limited-liability shield does not protect intentional fraud, unlawful distributions, abuse of the company, or personal guarantees.
Unlawful dividend distribution and profit repatriation

Statutory sanction: Unlawful distributions may be recoverable from shareholders who knew or should have known of the defect and from directors who authorized them. Additional Corporate Income Tax, withholding tax, interest, surcharges, and penalties may apply.

Director personal liability: Directors may be jointly liable for restitution and damages, lose management protection in insolvency, and face criminal exposure where the distribution is part of asset stripping or creditor prejudice.
